fluff.overview:
The Bombardier was proposed to the Star League in 2735 by Wakazashi Enterprises as a specialized sixty-five-ton fire support BattleMech designed to replace less-mobile artillery vehicles that might fall behind in an advance or be destroyed by counterbattery fire. The design used specialized missile racks capable of carrying diverse types of advanced munitions, filling the role of a mobile artillery platform that could keep pace with advancing BattleMech formations while delivering devastating long-range firepower.

The Bombardier's reputation has fluctuated dramatically over the centuries, from a promising Star League-era fire support platform to a near-extinct relic of the Succession Wars. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery have since revived the design, and the Bombardier's long-range fire support role has proven as relevant in the post-Jihad era as it was during the Star League.
fluff.capabilities:
The original BMB-12D mounts a pair of Delphinius-20 LRM launchers as its primary armament, weapons specifically designed to handle unique Star League-era ammunition types such as Swarm and Thunder missiles. A VOX 325 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour, allowing the Bombardier to keep pace with advancing formations and reposition as needed. Choutaka Armorscale protection with CASE provides solid defensive coverage for a fire support platform, and a Buzzsaw anti-missile system offers additional protection against incoming missile fire.

The Bombardier's greatest weakness is its limited endurance. With only two tons of LRM ammunition providing a mere twelve salvos, the design cannot sustain fire in an extended engagement. An Arrowlite-4 SRM launcher in the right arm provides some defense against units that close inside the LRMs' minimum effective range, but it carries only a single ton of ammunition and is insufficient to repel a determined assault. Unlike comparable fire support designs such as the Archer, the Bombardier carries no energy weapons to fall back on once its missile stores are depleted, leaving MechWarriors with a well-armored but toothless machine once the ammunition runs dry.
fluff.history:
The Bombardier's history is one of promise unfulfilled and unlikely resurrection. Proposed in 2735 by Wakazashi Enterprises on Al Na'ir, the design was conceived as a BattleMech replacement for conventional artillery vehicles, offering superior mobility and survivability while maintaining devastating long-range firepower. The Star League Defense Force embraced the concept, and the Bombardier performed admirably in exercises and limited deployments during the final decades of the Star League era. By the time of the Amaris Civil War and the subsequent Exodus, more than eight hundred Bombardiers were distributed across SLDF formations.

The Succession Wars proved catastrophic for the design. The specialized Bombardier Artillery Missiles that gave the chassis its name were consumed at staggering rates during the First Succession War, with many garrison worlds exhausting their entire stockpiles within days of sustained combat. Forced into close-support roles for which it was never designed, the Bombardier suffered the highest battlefield loss rate of any BattleMech type. Wakazashi's primary factory on Al Na'ir was destroyed during the First Succession War, and the company, increasingly focused on aerospace production, saw no reason to rebuild capacity for a design with such a poor battlefield reputation.

Earthwerks Incorporated on Calloway VI obtained a license from Wakazashi to produce spare parts and began refitting surviving Bombardiers into the simplified BMB-10D configuration during the late Succession Wars. These refits kept the design alive in small numbers, though most were consigned to militia garrisons or reserve formations in the Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine. The Federated Commonwealth assigned its Bombardiers to training cadres where their limited ammunition was a manageable constraint rather than a battlefield liability. The Delphinius LRM-20 launchers salvaged from surviving 12Ds found second lives as replacement components for Archers, Apollos, and Catapults, meaning that a working Bombardier in the field was often a sign that the unit fielding it was on its last legs.

The Bombardier's most dramatic chapter began with the Clan Invasion's aftermath. The Outworlds Alliance, long dismissed as a minor Periphery power, forged a partnership with Clan Snow Raven that transformed the Alliance's industrial base. A massive factory complex, Clan enclave, and DropShip repair facility appeared on Mitchella, and the United Outworlders Corporation began producing both new BMB-12Ds and the radically upgraded BMB-05A. When Alliance Grenadiers fielded these new Bombardiers during a raid against Enif, Combine intelligence agents took immediate notice. The once-timid Alliance was mass-producing effective fire support 'Mechs, prompting Wakazashi to begin refitting older Bombardier frames into the MML-equipped BMB-14K at facilities on Dover and New Samarkand.

ComStar's secret development of the BMB-14C added another thread to the design's revival, though the Word of Blake schism and subsequent Jihad left the fate of these machines uncertain. By the early thirty-second century, the Bombardier had gone from a design on the verge of extinction to one actively produced and refitted by multiple factions, its long-range fire support role proving as relevant in the post-Jihad era as it had been during the Star League.
fluff.deployment: This variant is a Succession Wars-era refit performed by Earthwerks Incorporated on their Calloway VI facility after Wakazashi licensed them to produce replacement parts. The advanced Delphinius and Arrowlite launchers were replaced with lower-technology Doombud LRM-20 and Hovertech SRM-4 models, and the Buzzsaw anti-missile system gave way to a Voelkers 200 machine gun. Most significantly, the VOX 325 XL engine was swapped for a smaller Magna 260, reducing top speed to just sixty-four kilometers per hour. The loss of CASE protection for the ammunition stores makes the 10D more vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions, though armor coverage remains unchanged. Communications and targeting systems were likewise downgraded to a Neil 5000 and RCA Instatrac Mark XII respectively. The 10D saw service primarily with Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine militia units, while the Federated Commonwealth relegated theirs to training academies where ammunition shortages were less problematic.
